_note: DEMO SEED. Every case is synthetic=true and proves the workflow only. Card texts inside positions are paraphrased premises of the synthetic position, not a rules reference. Replace with real reviewed cases through the Inbox.

deck.source: cw-wizard/world_deck_manifest.py (the user's purchase manifest; tournament provenance not recorded)

concepts.name: Phantom Dive counter math
concepts.definition: Before placing the 6 counters, write each benched target's remaining HP / 10 and spend counters where they complete Knock Outs.
concepts.notes: Demo wording. Replace with coach-validated wording.

concepts.name: Prize map T+2
concepts.definition: Plan this turn's Prize cards together with next turn's, so the two turns finish the game along more than one route.

concepts.name: Phantom Dive future-KO setup
concepts.definition: Counters that do not Knock Out now can still put a target into next turn's KO range; weigh that against Prizes banked now.

concepts.name: Information before commitment
concepts.definition: Take the free information (look, draw, search results) before the actions that commit resources.

concepts.name: Resource preservation
concepts.definition: Spend the cards you can recover or replace; keep the unique and unrecoverable ones.

concepts.name: Two-Prize bench liability
concepts.definition: Every benched Pokémon ex is a gust target worth 2 Prizes; count what the opponent needs before benching one.

cases.observed_state:
SYNTHETIC DEMO POSITION
Your Active: Dragapult ex, energy for Phantom Dive attached.
Phantom Dive (premise of this position): 200 damage to the opponent's Active Pokémon, and put 6 damage counters on the opponent's Benched Pokémon in any way you like.
Opponent Active: a Pokémon ex (2 Prizes) with 190 HP remaining.
Opponent Bench:
  B1 Basic (1 Prize) 30 HP remaining
  B2 Basic (1 Prize) 30 HP remaining
  B3 Stage 1 (1 Prize) 60 HP remaining
  B4 Basic Pokémon ex (2 Prizes) 210 HP remaining
No effect prevents damage or damage counters.
Prizes remaining: you 6, opponent 5.
cases.prompt: You attack with Phantom Dive. Which placement of the 6 counters takes the most Prize cards THIS turn?
cases.hint: One damage counter = 10 damage. Count counters needed per target.

choices.text: 2 on B1, 2 on B2, 2 on B3

evidence.claim: Active: 200 >= 190, KO (2 Prizes) in every option. B puts 30 damage on B1 and B2 (30 HP each): 2 more KOs, 4 Prizes total, the maximum possible with 6 counters here.
A: 60 damage KOs B3 only: 3 Prizes total.
C: B4 goes to 150 HP, no bench KO: 2 Prizes total.
D: 20 damage each, no bench KO: 2 Prizes total.
Whether taking the most Prizes now is the right plan depends on the rest of the game. This case only trains the counting.

cases.observed_state:
SYNTHETIC DEMO POSITION
Prizes remaining: you 5, opponent 3.
Your Active: Dragapult ex (Phantom Dive premise: 200 to the Active, 6 counters on the Bench as you like). Your Bench: Drakloak, Dreepy. No second attacker is ready.
Opponent Active: a Pokémon ex (2 Prizes) with 190 HP remaining: Phantom Dive KOs it.
Opponent Bench:
  B1 Basic (1 Prize) 30 HP remaining
  B4 Basic Pokémon ex (2 Prizes) 210 HP remaining, it will attack next turn
You have Boss's Orders in hand for next turn.
unknown_fields: whether the opponent can Knock Out your Dragapult ex next turn
cases.prompt: After the Active KO you will have 3 Prizes left. Where do the 6 counters go?
cases.hint: Write the Prizes you need next turn under each option.

evidence.claim: A leaves you at 2 Prizes: next turn a KO on B4 (180 HP) or on any two 1-Prize Pokémon wins. B leaves you at 3 Prizes: next turn B4 (150 HP) plus one 1-Prize KO wins.
A Prize taken now cannot be undone by healing, switching or shuffling; damage placed on B4 can.
If your Dragapult ex is Knocked Out and the next attacker hits for 150-179, A leaves B4 out of KO range; only B keeps it in.
Which heuristic applies depends on the opponent's hand and your backup attacker. This demo does not settle it.

cases.observed_state:
SYNTHETIC DEMO POSITION
Your turn 3. Active: Drakloak. Bench: Drakloak, Budew.
Drakloak ability (premise): once during your turn, look at the top 2 cards of your deck, put 1 into your hand and the other on the bottom.
Hand: Ultra Ball, Basic Fire Energy, Crushing Hammer, Night Stretcher, Boss's Orders.
You want a Dragapult ex this turn. Nothing has been played yet.
cases.hint: Which action tells you something for free?

choices.text: Ultra Ball first (discard 2) for Dragapult ex, then use the ability
Use the ability first, then decide on Ultra Ball and its discards
Attach Fire Energy first, then Ultra Ball

evidence.claim: Looking first can find the Dragapult ex or change which two cards you are willing to discard.
Discarding before looking can throw away a card the ability would have made unnecessary to spend.
Attachment order matters only if an attachment target decision depends on what you find; not settled here.

cases.observed_state:
SYNTHETIC DEMO POSITION
Prizes remaining: you 4, opponent 2.
Your board: Active Dragapult ex (ready to attack), Bench: Drakloak, Dreepy. No Pokémon ex on your Bench.
Hand: Meowth ex, Poké Pad, Basic Psychic Energy.
Meowth ex (premise): when you play it from your hand onto your Bench, you may search your deck for a Supporter.
You have no Supporter in hand. Your attack this turn takes 1 Prize at most.
unknown_fields: whether the opponent holds a gust effect
cases.prompt: Do you bench Meowth ex to find a Supporter?
cases.hint: What does the opponent need to win next turn in each case?

choices.text: Bench Meowth ex and search a Supporter
Do not bench Meowth ex; play Poké Pad and take the attack

evidence.claim: With 2 Prizes left, a benched Meowth ex is a one-gust win for the opponent.
If the Supporter found wins the game this turn or removes the opponent's win, the liability may not matter.
Whether the opponent holds a gust effect is hidden information.

cases.observed_state:
SYNTHETIC DEMO POSITION
Mid-game. Your Bench: Drakloak x2, no energy on either. Active: Budew.
Hand: Ultra Ball, Budew, Night Stretcher, Basic Psychic Energy, Basic Fire Energy, Boss's Orders.
Night Stretcher (premise): put a Pokémon or a Basic Energy from your discard pile into your hand.
You will Ultra Ball for Dragapult ex. You do not need to attack this turn.
cases.prompt: Which 2 cards do you discard to Ultra Ball?

choices.text: Basic Fire Energy + Basic Psychic Energy

evidence.claim: Budew and a Basic Energy are both recoverable with Night Stretcher; Boss's Orders and Night Stretcher are not.
Boss's Orders is a unique gust effect; discarding it early narrows later prize maps.
If both energy types are needed next turn and none remain in the deck, D can cost a turn. Energy remaining is unknown.
